citations.title: Home Care Services Consumer Protection Act
citations.requirement: Governing statute. The article list shows Art. 6 (licensure, §§1796.32-.41), Art. 7 (HCO operating requirements, §§1796.42-.43), Art. 8 (affiliated aides, §§1796.44-.45), Art. 10 (complaints/inspections, §§1796.51-.54), Art. 11 (enforcement, §§1796.55-.59). The sections fetched contain no staffing ratios, no client-rights or grievance rules, no records-retention period and no emergency-plan rule.

citations.title: Definitions
citations.requirement: (a) An affiliated home care aide is 18 or older, is EMPLOYED by an HCO, and is listed on the registry. (j) An HCO arranges home care services by an affiliated aide. (n) 'Home care services' are NON-MEDICAL services for a client who cannot perform them because of age or disability. They include bathing, dressing, feeding, exercising, hygiene/grooming, transferring, ambulating, positioning, toileting/incontinence care, assisting with self-administered medication, housekeeping, meals, laundry, transportation, correspondence, phone calls, shopping and companionship. Aides may NOT assist with medication that would otherwise require administration or oversight by a licensed health care professional. (i) The registry is a public CDSS website.

citations.title: Entities that are not home care organizations
citations.requirement: Exempts licensed home health agencies and hospices, IHSS providers, employment agencies referring independent aides, and DDS-vendored organizations (per research S9). Used to define who is and is not an HCO.

citations.title: HCO licensure requirements and two-year renewal
citations.requirement: (a)(2)-(4) Proof of $1M/$3M liability insurance, workers' compensation (policy number, dates, carrier name and address) and a $10,000 employee dishonesty bond with third-party coverage. (a)(5) On request, give CDSS a complete list of affiliated aides and proof each meets §§1796.43, .44 and .45. (a)(6) Licensee passes the §1796.33 background exam. (a)(7) Licensee completes the CDSS orientation. (a)(8) No outstanding fees or civil penalties. (a)(9)-(10) Disclose prior roles in licensed facilities and any discipline. (a)(11) Board members understand their duties. (a)(13) Cooperate with CDSS. (b) Renew every 2 years, fee postmarked on or before expiration. (c) CDSS mails a fee notice at least 60 days before the renewal date.

citations.title: Denial, suspension and revocation
citations.requirement: Grounds to deny, suspend or revoke an HCO license (carried from fact-checked research S12; section text not re-fetched in this pass).

citations.title: Posting of license and business hours
citations.requirement: Post the license, business hours and any other information CDSS requires at the place of business in a conspicuous location visible to both clients and affiliated aides.

citations.title: Workers' compensation
citations.requirement: Maintain and abide by a valid workers' compensation policy covering affiliated aides.

citations.title: Employee dishonesty bond
citations.requirement: Maintain and abide by an employee dishonesty bond, including third-party coverage, of at least $10,000.

citations.title: General and professional liability insurance
citations.requirement: Maintain proof of general and professional liability insurance of at least $1,000,000 per occurrence and $3,000,000 aggregate.

citations.title: Abuse reporting and report retention
citations.requirement: Report suspected or known dependent adult/elder abuse as required by WIC §15630. Report suspected or known child abuse as required by Penal Code §§11164-11174.3. Keep a copy of EACH suspected-abuse report, available to CDSS for review during normal business hours.

citations.title: Registry clearance before client contact; staff clearance; TB; notice on separation
citations.requirement: Aides must be cleared on the registry before direct client contact. (a)(1) Any staff person, volunteer or employee with contact with clients, prospective clients or confidential client information must satisfy §§1796.23, .24, .25, .26 and .28 BEFORE that contact or access. (a)(2) Aides must show they are free of active TB under §1796.45. (b) The licensee may require criminal record clearance of exempt individuals who have client contact.

citations.title: Notify CDSS when an aide is no longer employed
citations.requirement: Immediately notify the department when the HCO no longer employs an individual as an affiliated home care aide.

citations.cite: HSC §1796.44(a)-(d) (in effect through 12/31/2026; reenacted by SB 412, Stats. 2025, ch. 414)
citations.title: Affiliated home care aide training
citations.requirement: The licensee must ensure each aide completes training BEFORE providing services. (b) Minimum 5 hours entry-level training before presence with a client: 2 hours orientation on the aide's role and the terms of employment, and 3 hours safety (basic safety precautions, emergency procedures, infection control). (c) Plus a minimum 5 hours of annual training, core-competency and population-specific. It must include clients' rights and safety, daily living needs, reporting/preventing/detecting abuse and neglect, personal hygiene help, and safe transport if transportation is provided. (d) Training may be online.

citations.title: Dementia training added to annual training
citations.requirement: From 1/1/2027 the annual training must also cover the special care needs of clients with dementia. The 5-hour entry and 5-hour annual minimums are unchanged. The bill digest also describes dementia training prior to providing care and annually thereafter; the chaptered §1796.44(c)(6) text lists it in the annual training. Counsel should confirm whether a pre-service dementia component is required.

citations.title: Tuberculosis examination of aides
citations.requirement: (a) Aides hired on or after 1/1/2016 must be examined 90 days before employment or within 7 days after. (b) The exam is a CDC-recommended, FDA-licensed TB infection test and, if positive, a chest X-ray. The aide may not work unless the licensee has documentation from a licensed medical professional of no risk of spreading disease. (c) Repeat at least every 2 years if negative. Once a positive test has been followed by an X-ray, repeat exams are no longer required. (d) After each exam the aide submits, and the HCO keeps on file, the practitioner's certificate. (e) The exam is a condition of initial and continuing employment. (f) A transferring aide meets the requirement with a certificate from within the past 2 years, or verification from the prior HCO that it holds the certificate and a copy is provided before the aide starts.

citations.title: License fees
citations.requirement: Initial (24-month) and renewal fees set by the department. Current schedule per CDSS (research S2): HCO license $5,603 per 2 years, change of location $100, change in corporation $200, aide registration $35.

citations.title: Complaint procedures
citations.requirement: CDSS may establish procedures for the receipt, investigation and resolution of complaints against HCOs.

citations.title: Inspections, complaint investigations, abuse cross-reporting
citations.requirement: (a) CDSS may investigate complaints. (b) CDSS verifies compliance through random, unannounced inspections. (c) Inspections may cover books, records and premises. Refusing access is cause for license revocation. (d) CDSS has no oversight of registered aides other than maintaining the registry. (e) On receipt of an abuse report under §1796.42(e), CDSS cross-reports to local law enforcement and APS (adult victim) or CPS (child victim). It has no duty to investigate beyond that.

citations.title: Department entry during business hours
citations.requirement: CDSS may enter an HCO during posted business hours, with or without advance notice (per research S49).

citations.title: Elder and dependent adult abuse mandated reporting
citations.requirement: (a) Persons with full or intermittent responsibility for the care or custody of an elder or dependent adult, whether or not paid, including any elder or dependent adult care custodian, are mandated reporters. (b)(1) Report observed, known or reasonably suspected physical abuse, abandonment, abduction, isolation, financial abuse or neglect, or abuse disclosed by the elder/dependent adult. Report by telephone or confidential internet tool immediately or as soon as practicably possible. A written or internet report follows within 2 working days. (b)(1)(F) For abuse outside a long-term care facility, the report goes to the adult protective services agency or local law enforcement.

citations.title: Paid sick leave
citations.requirement: Paid sick leave of at least 40 hours / 5 days per year (per research S36).

citations.title: Employer indemnification of employee expenses
citations.requirement: The employer must reimburse necessary employee expenditures, including mileage for driving between clients and on client errands (per research S37). The 2026 IRS rate is 72.5 cents per mile (S38), a common benchmark.

citations.title: Third-party employers and the companionship/live-in exemptions
citations.requirement: Third-party employers of home care workers, including HCOs, may not claim the FLSA companionship or live-in exemptions from minimum wage and overtime.

citations.title: Electronic visit verification for Medicaid personal care services
citations.requirement: EVV is required for Medicaid-funded personal care services. It applies only to Medi-Cal-funded visits. Confirm the system with DHCS or the managed care plan.

citations.cite: CDSS HCS 281 — Application Instructions for an HCO License (Sections A and B)
citations.title: Required application content: personnel policies, training plan, job descriptions, program description, HCS 308 designee
citations.requirement: B2 job descriptions for each position. B3 personnel policies covering hiring, discipline, grievance and mandated reporting, stating that employment is conditional on fingerprint clearance, a criminal-conviction statement, TB clearance and registry listing. B4 training plan with trainers, objectives and a sample log. B5 program description (services, area, hours, population, assignment/supervision). B6 insurance certificates. HCS 308: at least one designee, and a licensee cannot designate him/herself; LLC/corporations attach a board resolution. HCS 402 bond.

citations.cite: CDSS Home Care Services application fees and HCO/HCA application pages
citations.title: Fees, forms, HCSB and Care Provider Management Branch contacts
citations.requirement: HCO license $5,603 per 2 years; change of location $100; change in corporation $200; aide registration $35 per 2 years and $35 renewal. HCSB: (877) 424-5778, HCSB@dss.ca.gov, 744 P Street, M.S. 9-14-90, Sacramento, CA 95814. Aide Live Scan/registration via the Guardian portal (Care Provider Management Branch 1-888-422-5669, guardian@dss.ca.gov).

citations.cite: CDSS/DHCS joint notice (Dec. 16, 2021) — Medi-Cal Personal Care Agencies serving the HCBA Waiver
citations.title: HCBA Waiver Personal Care Agency exemption from HCO licensure
citations.requirement: Medi-Cal Personal Care Agencies providing HCBA Waiver Personal Care Services are exempt from HCO licensure. An HCO that is not enrolled for the waiver is not covered by this exemption.

citations.cite: DHCS Community Supports Policy Guide, Vol. 1 (updated April 2025) — Personal Care and Homemaker Services (PCHS)
citations.title: Medi-Cal managed care Community Supports
citations.requirement: PCHS is a plan-offered Community Support. It covers eligibility, IHSS as the primary program, HCBA exclusion and provider types. Plans contract with and pay providers. Pricing benchmark (non-binding) $29/$33/$38 per hour (research S19).

policies.title: Organization, Licensee, Designee and Administrator Responsibilities
state_specifics: The licensee is the individual or entity with authority and responsibility for operating the HCO (§1796.12(m)). The licensee must pass the CDSS background exam and complete the CDSS orientation (§1796.37(a)(6)-(7)).
Name at least one designee on HCS 308 to act in the licensee's absence. A licensee cannot designate him/herself. LLCs and corporations attach a board resolution (HCS 281).

The Act sets no administrator license, RN requirement or staffing ratio. Do not state any in the manual. Define the owner, designee, care supervisor and scheduler roles by job description (HCS 281 B2).
Board members, if any, sign HCS 9165 before joining and understand that CDSS enforces the Act (§1796.37(a)(11)). Keep the signed forms on file.
Disclose prior roles as administrator, officer, director, general partner or 10%+ owner of community care, residential care, child day care or HCO licensees, and any discipline (§1796.37(a)(9)-(10)).
Keep no outstanding CDSS fees or civil penalties (§1796.37(a)(8)). Respond to CDSS requests promptly (§1796.37(a)(13)).

policies.title: Licensure, Service Area and Advertising Requirements
state_specifics: An HCO license is required to arrange non-medical home care services by employed, registered aides (§1796.12(j),(n)). Exemptions are listed in §1796.17. HCBA Waiver Personal Care Agencies are exempt only for that waiver service (C27).

The license term is 2 years. Renew by postmarking the nonrefundable fee on or before the expiration date; CDSS mails a fee notice at least 60 days before (§1796.37(b)-(c)). Current fee $5,603; $100 for a change of location and $200 for a change in corporation (CDSS fee page).
Use the HCO number on all CDSS correspondence. The HCSB contact is (877) 424-5778 or HCSB@dss.ca.gov.
Advertise and describe only non-medical services. Do not offer skilled nursing, therapy, or medication that requires a licensed professional (§1796.12(n)).
The sections fetched contain no HCO-specific advertising or service-area rule. Define the service area in the program description (HCS 281 B5) and have counsel review advertising claims.

policies.title: Policy Review and Document Control
state_specifics: The personnel policies, training plan, job descriptions and program description are submitted with the application (HCS 281 B2-B5). Version-control them and keep a dated copy of whatever CDSS last received.
Add the dementia topic to the annual training content before 1/1/2027 (SB 412). Record the revision in the change log.
Review the manual at least annually and whenever statute changes. The annual cycle is an operator choice, not a state mandate.
Keep the manual and training logs available for CDSS inspection (§1796.52(c)).

policies.title: Quality Assurance and Performance Improvement
state_specifics: No state QA or QAPI rule applies to HCOs. This policy is operator-adopted.

Run internal audits mirroring what CDSS checks in random unannounced inspections (§1796.52(b)): registry status, clearance, TB certificate currency, entry and annual training logs, insurance and bond in force, abuse-report copies, and posted license and hours.
Track missed visits, complaints, supervisory-visit completion and aide turnover. Report results to the licensee at least quarterly (suggested).

policies.title: Corporate Compliance, Fraud and Billing Integrity
federal: 31 U.S.C. §3729 (False Claims Act — applies if Medi-Cal/Medicaid funds are billed)
state_specifics: Grounds for denial, suspension or revocation are in §1796.38. The employee dishonesty bond (≥$10,000, with third-party coverage) is a statutory requirement (§1796.42(c)).

Bill only for hours actually worked, verified by timekeeping or EVV. Medi-Cal-funded hours go through the managed care plan contract. Plans negotiate rates; the DHCS $29/$33/$38 hourly benchmark is non-binding.
Private-pay invoices must match the service agreement rates and the timekeeping records.
Set an internal reporting channel and non-retaliation rule for billing concerns (operator best practice).

policies.title: Required Insurance, Employee Dishonesty Bond and Postings
state_specifics: Keep in force at all times: general and professional liability of at least $1M per occurrence and $3M aggregate (§1796.42(d)); workers' compensation covering affiliated aides (§1796.42(b)); employee dishonesty bond with third-party coverage of at least $10,000 (§1796.42(c)). The bond is on HCS 402 with the State of California as beneficiary (HCS 281).
Proof of workers' compensation shows the policy number, effective and expiration dates, and carrier name and address (§1796.37(a)(3)).
Post the license, business hours and any other CDSS-required information conspicuously where clients and aides can see them (§1796.42(a)).
Assign a person to diary expiration dates and keep current certificates on file. A lapse violates operating requirements.

policies.title: CDSS Inspections, Complaint Investigations and Enforcement Response
state_specifics: CDSS conducts random, unannounced inspections and may investigate complaints (§1796.52(a)-(b)). It may enter during posted business hours with or without advance notice (§1796.53).

Inspection may cover books, records and premises. Refusing to make records, books or premises available is cause for license revocation (§1796.52(c)). Instruct all office staff to give inspectors immediate access and to notify the designee.
Keep on-site or immediately retrievable: aide roster with registry, clearance, TB and training proof (§1796.37(a)(5)); insurance and bond; copies of abuse reports (§1796.42(e)).
Log each inspection or complaint inquiry, the findings and the corrective action. CDSS has no oversight of aides other than the registry (§1796.52(d)).

policies.title: Client Rights and Responsibilities
state_specifics: The Act contains no client bill of rights. Adopt one as a policy and give it to every client at intake.
Annual aide training must cover 'clients' rights and safety' (§1796.44(c)(1)). Teach this policy there.

Suggested content (operator-adopted): dignity and respect, freedom from abuse, neglect and exploitation, privacy, informed participation in the service plan, right to refuse services, right to know the aide's registry status, and how to complain to the HCO and to CDSS HCSB (877) 424-5778.
Document delivery with a signed acknowledgment.

policies.title: Grievances and Complaints
state_specifics: HCS 281 B3 requires personnel policies that include a grievance procedure. Keep the client complaint procedure consistent with it.
Tell clients they may complain to CDSS HCSB at (877) 424-5778 or HCSB@dss.ca.gov. CDSS may establish procedures for receiving and resolving complaints (§1796.51) and may investigate (§1796.52(a)).
Complaint acknowledgment and resolution time frames are not set by statute. Use an operator standard, e.g. acknowledge within 2 business days and resolve in writing within 30 days (suggested).
Complaints that allege abuse or neglect also go to SAF-01. Never retaliate against a complaining client or employee.

policies.title: Privacy, Confidentiality and HIPAA
state_specifics: Staff, volunteers and employees with access to confidential client information must satisfy the §1796.43(a)(1) clearance requirements before access.

HIPAA applies directly if the HCO is a covered entity, for example if it conducts standard electronic transactions with health plans. Otherwise adopt the HIPAA standards by policy. Decide and document covered-entity status with counsel.
California medical-privacy statutes (e.g., CMIA) and breach-notice law are not verified here. Have counsel add the section citations.

Rules: share client information only as needed for care, billing or as legally required (abuse reports are permitted and required). Keep paper records locked and use password-protected systems. Do not discuss clients on social media.

policies.title: Client Property, Gifts and Financial Exploitation Prevention
state_specifics: WIC §15630 lists financial abuse as reportable. Suspected financial exploitation by anyone, including staff, is a mandated report.
The third-party coverage on the $10,000 employee dishonesty bond (§1796.42(c)) is the statutory backstop for employee theft. It does not replace controls.

Aides may shop for groceries and personal care items (§1796.12(n)). Controls (operator-adopted): receipts for every purchase, no use of client cards or PINs, no loans, no gifts of value, no being named in a client's will or powers of attorney, and no handling of cash beyond errand funds logged on a form.
Report any suspected theft to the client or representative and the designee the same day.

policies.title: Nondiscrimination and Language Access
federal: Title VI, 42 U.S.C. §2000d (if the HCO receives federal financial assistance)
state_specifics: No HCO-specific nondiscrimination or language-access rule appears in the Act sections fetched. California civil rights statutes are not verified here.

Serve clients without discrimination by race, color, national origin, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, disability, age or source of payment, subject to the service area and scope of services.
Provide interpreter or translated-document access. Include communication needs in intake. Provide reasonable accommodations for clients with disabilities.
Train aides on respectful, culturally competent care within 'clients' rights' training (§1796.44(c)(1)).

policies.title: Service Agreement, Rates and Billing Disclosure
state_specifics: The Act does not prescribe service agreement terms. The contents below are operator best practice.
Before services start, give the client a written agreement with services, schedule, hourly rate and minimum visit length, cancellation terms, billing cycle, and how to complain to HCO and CDSS.
State that the HCO employs the aides (affiliated aides) and that they are registered with CDSS.
Because third-party employers cannot use the FLSA companionship exemption (29 CFR §552.109), do not offer flat-rate live-in or 24-hour pricing before counsel reviews California overtime rules.
Medi-Cal plan-funded clients: rates and authorizations come from the plan contract, not private-pay terms.

policies.title: Scope of Services — What Aides May and May Not Do
state_specifics: Permitted non-medical services (§1796.12(n)): bathing, dressing, feeding, exercising, personal hygiene and grooming, transferring, ambulating, positioning, toileting and incontinence care, assisting with self-administered medication, housekeeping, meal planning and preparation, laundry, transportation, correspondence, phone calls, shopping for personal care items or groceries, and companionship.

Prohibited: skilled nursing or therapy, administering medication, or any medication help that would otherwise require administration or oversight by a licensed health care professional (§1796.12(n)). These belong to home health agencies and other licensees (§1796.17).
Refer client requests outside scope to the care supervisor. Do not make exceptions in the field.
The scope is limited to clients who 'because of advanced age or physical or mental disability' cannot perform the tasks themselves (§1796.12(n)).

policies.title: Client Intake, Eligibility and Assessment
state_specifics: Accept only clients whose needs can be met by non-medical home care within the HCO's program description (HCS 281 B5).

The Act prescribes no assessment form or timeline. Use an in-home assessment before the first visit (operator standard): ADLs, cognition and dementia, mobility, home safety, medications used, emergency contacts, physician and representative, and language needs.
Screen for needs requiring a licensed provider (wounds, injections, skilled care) and refer them (§1796.12(n)).
Confirm the payer: private pay, long-term care insurance, or Medi-Cal plan Community Supports (PCHS). IHSS recipients may use the HCO privately for hours beyond their IHSS authorization.

policies.title: Service Plan and Plan Updates
state_specifics: The Act sets no service plan content or review interval. Write a plan from the assessment listing tasks by §1796.12(n) category, schedule, preferences and safety precautions.
Give aides the plan before the first visit. Aides must complete entry-level training before presence with a client (§1796.44(b)).
Update on a change in condition, at each supervisory visit, and at least every 6 months (suggested). Get the client's or representative's signature on each version.

policies.title: Supervision of Caregivers and Supervisory Visits
state_specifics: No supervisor ratio, credential or supervisory-visit frequency is set by the Act. The program description must state how aides are assigned and supervised (HCS 281 B5).
Operator standard: client care supervisor makes a first-visit check within the first week, then supervisory visits or calls at least every 90 days, with documentation.
CDSS has no oversight of individual registered aides beyond the registry (§1796.52(d)). The HCO as employer is accountable for supervision.

policies.title: Medication Assistance and Self-Administration Support
state_specifics: Aides may assist only with medication the client self-administers (§1796.12(n)). They may not assist with medication that would otherwise require administration or oversight by a licensed health care professional.

Define allowed acts in a short list, e.g. verbal reminders and handing the client a container the client opens and takes. Define forbidden acts: filling pill organizers, injections, adjusting doses, crushing pills, giving PRN medications by judgment, and applying medicated treatments requiring clinical judgment. The Act does not itemize these. Have counsel and the care supervisor finalize the list.

Document every assistance on a medication assistance log. Record refusals and report errors, missed doses and adverse reactions to the supervisor immediately and to the client's physician or 911 as appropriate (SVC-08).

policies.title: Scheduling, Missed Visits and Continuity of Care
state_specifics: Assign only aides who are cleared on the registry, have a TB certificate on file and have completed 5 hours of entry-level training (§§1796.43, .44, .45).
Travel between clients is paid work time (DOL WHD guidance; see PER-10). Schedule realistic travel time.

No statutory missed-visit rule applies. Operator standard: the scheduler calls the client and sends a replacement or notifies the client within 30 minutes of a late or no-show aide, and logs it. Escalate any client who cannot be left alone.

policies.title: Electronic Visit Verification and Timekeeping (Medi-Cal-funded services; internal timekeeping for all clients)
state_specifics: Federal law requires EVV for Medicaid personal care services. Confirm the required EVV system, data elements and any deadlines with each Medi-Cal managed care plan or DHCS before billing Community Supports services.

Private-pay visits are not subject to EVV by the Act. Still record actual clock-in, clock-out, location and tasks for payroll, billing and defense of overtime claims, since HCOs cannot claim the FLSA companionship exemption (29 CFR §552.109).
Aides record time contemporaneously. Supervisors review exceptions weekly, and edits require a documented reason.

policies.title: Change in Client Condition and Emergencies in the Home
state_specifics: Entry-level safety training must cover emergency procedures (§1796.44(b)(2)). Aides call 911 first for life-threatening emergencies, then the supervisor.

Aides do not diagnose or treat. They report changes (falls, confusion, new pain, skin changes, refused meals) to the supervisor the same day. The supervisor notifies the client's representative and physician.
If a condition suggests abuse or neglect, follow SAF-01 (WIC §15630).
If needs now exceed non-medical scope, follow SVC-09 and refer to a licensed provider.

policies.title: Discharge, Transfer and Discontinuation of Services
state_specifics: The Act has no discharge-notice rule for HCOs. Terms belong in the service agreement (CR-06).

Operator standard: written notice with reasons and referrals to other providers, at least 14 days where safe. Immediate discontinuation is allowed for safety threats to aides, non-payment after notice, or needs beyond non-medical scope.
Do not abandon a client with unmet safety needs. Where a client is at risk, notify the representative and, if warranted, APS (WIC §15630).
Document the discharge summary and close the record (RR-01).

policies.title: Coordination with Medi-Cal Managed Care Plans (Community Supports), IHSS and Other Payers
state_specifics: IHSS pays individual providers selected by the consumer through state payroll, not agencies (research S21-S22), and IHSS providers are not HCOs (§1796.17). Contract mode exists only in San Francisco.

Medi-Cal Community Supports Personal Care and Homemaker Services (PCHS) are authorized and paid by each managed care plan under its contract. Follow plan authorization, rate and claims rules. The DHCS pricing benchmark is non-binding.
Medi-Cal PCAs serving the HCBA Waiver are exempt from HCO licensure (C27). An HCO is not covered by that exemption.
Medi-Cal provider enrollment (PAVE) is needed only if a plan requires it. Coordinate with IHSS or the plan when a client receives other hours.

policies.title: Dementia Care Practices and Training Readiness (effective 1/1/2027)
state_specifics: From 1/1/2027, annual aide training must include the special care needs of clients with dementia (§1796.44(c)(6), SB 412, Stats. 2025, ch. 414). The 5-hour annual minimum stays unchanged.

The SB 412 digest also refers to dementia training 'prior to providing home care'. The chaptered text lists it only under annual training. Counsel should confirm; the conservative approach is to include dementia content in the 3-hour entry safety block or in the first annual module for aides assigned to dementia clients.
Document dementia status at intake. Assign trained aides. Use a safety plan for wandering, refusal of care and sundowning.

policies.title: Abuse, Neglect and Exploitation Prevention and Reporting (Elder and Dependent Adults)
state_specifics: Required by §1796.42(e) and WIC §15630. All staff with care responsibility for an elder or dependent adult are mandated reporters (WIC §15630(a)).
Report known, suspected or alleged physical abuse, abandonment, abduction, isolation, financial abuse or neglect. This includes abuse disclosed by the client (§15630(b)(1)).

Make the report by telephone or the confidential internet tool immediately or as soon as practicably possible. A written or internet report follows within 2 working days. For abuse in the client's home, report to the county adult protective services agency or local law enforcement (§15630(b)(1)(F)).

The HCO must keep a copy of each suspected-abuse report, available to CDSS during normal business hours (§1796.42(e)). CDSS cross-reports receipts to law enforcement and APS but does not replace the HCO's own report (§1796.52(e)).
Each mandated reporter has an individual duty. The employer may not impede or screen the report, so do not require supervisor approval before reporting.
The annual training must cover how to report, prevent and detect abuse and neglect (§1796.44(c)(3)).
Look up the county APS number and post it in the office and in the aide handbook (not verified here).

policies.title: Reporting Suspected Child Abuse in the Home
state_specifics: The HCO must report suspected or known child abuse as required by Penal Code §§11164 to 11174.3 and keep a copy of each report for CDSS review (§1796.42(e)).
The specific reporting time limits, agencies and forms under those Penal Code sections were not fetched. Counsel should insert them before publication.
Keep copies with the abuse reports. Annual training covers abuse reporting (§1796.44(c)(3)).

policies.title: Incident Reporting
state_specifics: The Act does not set a general incident-report requirement for HCOs. The only statutory reports in the sections fetched are suspected-abuse reports (§1796.42(e)) and aide separation notices (§1796.43(a)(3)). This policy is operator-adopted beyond those.
Define reportable incidents: falls, injuries, hospitalization, property loss or damage, medication events, client death, aide injury, allegations against staff, and aide or vehicle accidents.
Aides notify the supervisor immediately and complete a written incident report within 24 hours (operator standard). Supervisors notify the representative and review trends.
Aide injuries also follow PER-12 (workers' compensation).

policies.title: Infection Prevention and Control
state_specifics: Entry-level safety training must include infection control (§1796.44(b)(2)).
Each aide shows freedom from active TB (§1796.45) before working and every 2 years after, unless a positive test was followed by an X-ray.

OSHA bloodborne pathogens standard (29 CFR 1910.1030) applies to employees with occupational exposure. Provide gloves and PPE, a hand hygiene protocol, a sharps and soiled-linen protocol, an exposure incident procedure and hepatitis B vaccine offer where required.
Aides do not work while symptomatic with contagious illness. Cal/OSHA-specific standards are not verified here.

policies.title: Client Emergency and Disaster Plans
state_specifics: No HCO-specific disaster-plan rule appears in the Act sections fetched. Entry safety training must cover emergency procedures (§1796.44(b)(2)). Do not cite any Title 22 or CMS emergency preparedness rule for this program.

Operator standard: at intake rate each client's disaster risk (oxygen, mobility, cognitive impairment), record emergency contacts and evacuation help, and keep a prioritized call list for wildfire, earthquake, power shutoff and heat events.
Give the office an after-hours coordinator line. Plan backup staffing for disasters.

policies.title: Caregiver Safety in the Home and Workplace Violence
state_specifics: Safety training is required at entry (§1796.44(b)(2)). Workers' compensation must cover aides (§1796.42(b)).

California workplace violence prevention and Injury and Illness Prevention Program obligations apply to employers. Applicability and section numbers for HCOs are not verified here. Counsel should insert them.

Aides may leave an unsafe situation, including a hostile household member, weapons or aggression, and call 911 and the supervisor. Provide a no-retaliation rule, a safe-lifting protocol and a no-lone-lift rule for dependent transfers.

policies.title: Transporting Clients
state_specifics: Transportation is an HCO service (§1796.12(n)). If transportation is provided, annual training must cover how to safely transport a client (§1796.44(c)(5)).
Reimburse mileage for client transport and errands (Labor Code §2802). The 2026 IRS rate of 72.5 cents per mile is a common benchmark.

Require a valid license, registration and insurance for any aide who drives. Specific California vehicle-insurance limits are not verified here. Have counsel and the insurer confirm that the HCO's liability coverage and the aide's personal auto coverage apply.
Prohibit transporting clients in unsafe conditions, using a phone while driving, or transporting wheelchair users without proper securement training.

policies.title: Registered Home Care Aide Qualifications and Registry Listing
state_specifics: California uses 'registered home care aide', not 'certification'. An affiliated aide is 18 or older, employed by the HCO, and listed on the CDSS Home Care Aide Registry (§1796.12(a)). The registry is a public CDSS website (§1796.12(i)).
Aides must be cleared on the registry before direct contact with clients (§1796.43(a)).

Registration is online through the Guardian portal, or by HCS 100 by mail. The fee is $35 per 2 years, with a $35 renewal. Affiliated aides enter the HCO's PIN. Care Provider Management Branch: 1-888-422-5669.
The Act sets no minimum education or experience, and no state competency exam. Use job descriptions (HCS 281 B2).
Verify the registry status of each aide at hire, before assignment, and at each renewal.

policies.title: Background Checks and Employee Registries
state_specifics: Aides must be cleared on the registry before direct client contact. Staff, volunteers and employees with client or prospective-client contact, or access to confidential client information, must satisfy §§1796.23, .24, .25, .26 and .28 before that contact (§1796.43(a)(1)). The content of those sections was not fetched.
Applicants are fingerprinted by Live Scan through CDSS (Guardian). The licensee must pass the §1796.33 background exam (§1796.37(a)(6)).
Employment is conditional on fingerprint clearance, a statement of prior convictions, TB clearance and registry listing (HCS 281 B3). Criminal record statement form LIC 508.
A licensee may require criminal clearance of exempt individuals who have client contact (§1796.43(b)).
Check CDSS clearance status and registry status before the first shift. Do not assign an aide whose status is pending or not cleared.

policies.title: Orientation, Competency Evaluation and Annual Training
state_specifics: Before presence with a client every aide completes at least 5 hours: 2 hours orientation on the aide's role and the terms of employment, and 3 hours safety covering basic safety precautions, emergency procedures and infection control (§1796.44(b)).

Every aide then completes at least 5 hours of annual training that is core-competency and population-specific, covering: clients' rights and safety; daily living needs; reporting, preventing and detecting abuse and neglect; personal hygiene and other home care services; and safe transport if transportation is provided (§1796.44(c)).
From 1/1/2027 annual training must also include dementia care (§1796.44(c)(6)).
Training may be online (§1796.44(d)).
The training plan names trainers and objectives and includes a sample training log (HCS 281 B4). Keep a training log per aide.
The Act has no state competency exam. Run a skills check-off (operator standard) for transfers, incontinence care and safe lifting.

policies.title: Employee Health and TB Screening
state_specifics: Each aide hired on or after 1/1/2016 must be examined 90 days before employment or within 7 days after (§1796.45(a)). The exam is a CDC-recommended, FDA-licensed TB infection test and, if positive, a chest X-ray (§1796.45(b)).
The aide may not work unless the HCO has documentation from a licensed medical professional that there is no risk of spreading the disease (§1796.45(b)).
Repeat at least every 2 years if negative. No repeat is required after a documented positive test followed by an X-ray (§1796.45(c)).
Keep the practitioner's certificate on file after each exam (§1796.45(d)). The exam is a condition of initial and continuing employment (§1796.45(e)).
A transferring aide meets the requirement with a certificate from within the past 2 years, or verified from the prior HCO, before starting (§1796.45(f)).
Offer no other health screening requirements unless counsel confirms them.

policies.title: Personnel Records
state_specifics: Keep per aide: registry status and PIN, Live Scan clearance, TB certificate(s), entry and annual training logs, signed criminal-conviction statement, I-9 and payroll records.
On CDSS request the HCO must provide a complete aide list and proof each aide meets §§1796.43, .44 and .45 (§1796.37(a)(5)).
The Act sets no retention period. Adopt a retention schedule with counsel (California Labor Code record rules not verified here). TB certificates must stay on file (§1796.45(d)).
Keep personnel files confidential, separate from client records, and available for CDSS inspection (§1796.52(c)).

policies.title: Wage, Hour and Overtime Compliance
state_specifics: HCOs are third-party employers and may not claim the FLSA companionship or live-in exemptions (29 CFR §552.109). Pay minimum wage and overtime for all hours worked.

2026 California minimum wage is $16.90. Local minimums are higher in many cities, for example City of Los Angeles $18.42 and unincorporated LA County $18.47 (from 7/1/2026), San Francisco $19.61, San Diego $17.75, San Jose $18.45, West Hollywood $20.25 and Emeryville $20.34. Pay the higher of state and local rates.
SB 525 health-care minimum wage covers licensed home health agencies. HCOs are not listed (research S32). Confirm with counsel.
California daily overtime, meal and rest break, and live-in or 24-hour shift rules were not verified here. Counsel must confirm before offering live-in care.
Paid sick leave: see PER-09. Travel time and mileage: see PER-10.

policies.title: Staff Conduct and Professional Boundaries
state_specifics: Personnel policies must cover discipline and mandated reporting (HCS 281 B3).

Rules: no accepting gifts, loans or financial benefit; no personal use of client property; no soliciting clients to hire the aide privately; no social-media posts about clients; no use of drugs or alcohol on duty; no visitors in the client's home.
Violations of abuse-reporting duty and client exploitation are grounds for immediate suspension and termination (SAF-01, CR-04).

policies.title: Employment Status of Aides — W-2 Employees Only
state_specifics: An affiliated aide is 'employed by' the HCO (§1796.12(a)); an HCO arranges services by affiliated aides (§1796.12(j)). Independent aides are those who contract directly with a client (§1796.12(p)), which is not the HCO model.
Do not classify aides as independent contractors. Do not use the companionship or live-in exemptions (29 CFR §552.109).
Employer payroll costs per research: FICA 7.65%, UI 3.4% for a new employer and ETT 0.1% on the first $7,000 per employee. Employees pay SDI 1.3% (research S33-S34).

policies.title: Paid Sick Leave and Leaves of Absence
state_specifics: Provide at least 40 hours or 5 days of paid sick leave per year (Labor Code §246). Include accrual, carryover, use and no-retaliation terms.
Do not require an aide with symptoms of a contagious illness to work (SAF-04). Other leave laws were not verified here.

policies.title: Travel Time, Mileage and Expense Reimbursement
state_specifics: Travel between clients during the workday is compensable time (DOL WHD direct care travel-time guidance, research S39).
Reimburse necessary expenditures, including mileage for driving between clients and on client errands (Labor Code §2802). The 2026 IRS rate is 72.5 cents per mile (research S38).
Record mileage by client and date on a log. Pay within the next regular payroll.

policies.title: Separation of Aides and Notice to CDSS
state_specifics: Immediately notify CDSS when the HCO no longer employs an individual as an affiliated aide (§1796.43(a)(3)). The research indicates this can be done through the HCO's Guardian account. Confirm the current method with Care Provider Management Branch (1-888-422-5669).
Keep the aide's TB certificate and training logs. A transferring aide may give them to the next HCO (§1796.45(f)).
Retrieve keys, ID badges and client information on the last day.

policies.title: Workers' Compensation and Employee Injury Reporting
state_specifics: Maintain and abide by a valid workers' compensation policy covering affiliated aides (§1796.42(b)). Proof includes policy number, dates and carrier name and address (§1796.37(a)(3)).

Aides report every work injury to the supervisor the same day. The HCO provides the claim form, notifies the carrier, and records the incident (SAF-03). California claim-form and employer-report deadlines were not verified here.

policies.title: Clearance of Office Staff, Schedulers, Supervisors and Volunteers
state_specifics: Any staff person, volunteer or employee who has contact with clients or prospective clients, or confidential client information that may pose a risk to client health and safety, must meet §§1796.23, .24, .25, .26 and .28 before that contact or access (§1796.43(a)(1)).
Apply this to schedulers, care supervisors, intake staff and billing staff with client data access. Do not let uncleared staff view client files or call clients.
The Act does not state a credential for supervisors or schedulers. Job descriptions are required (HCS 281 B2).

policies.title: Client Records and Retention
federal: 45 CFR 164.530(j) (six-year documentation retention, if a HIPAA covered entity)
state_specifics: The Act sets no client-record content or retention period. This policy is operator-adopted.
Record: assessment, service plan and updates, signed agreement and rights acknowledgment, visit and task notes, medication logs, supervisory visits, incident reports and complaint files.
Keep the copies of suspected-abuse reports (§1796.42(e)) so they are available to CDSS in normal business hours. CDSS may inspect books and records (§1796.52(c)).
Set a retention period with counsel. A common choice is at least 7 years after discharge. This is not a state mandate.
Store records securely and control access (CR-03).

policies.title: Required Reports and Notices to the State
state_specifics: Abuse reports to APS or law enforcement under WIC §15630 and to authorities under Penal Code §§11164-11174.3, with copies kept (§1796.42(e)).
Immediate notice to CDSS when an aide is no longer employed (§1796.43(a)(3)).
Aide list and proof of compliance on CDSS request (§1796.37(a)(5)).
License renewal every 2 years with the fee postmarked by expiration (§1796.37(b)); $100 for a change of location and $200 for a change in corporation (CDSS fee page).
Respond promptly to CDSS requests. Failure to cooperate can lead to withdrawal of an application or expiration or denial of renewal (§1796.37(a)(13), (b)(4)).
No periodic statistical or incident reports to CDSS were found in the Act.

policies.title: Aide Roster, Registry Status and Proof of Compliance on Request
state_specifics: Maintain a current roster of all affiliated aides with registry number and status, clearance date, TB exam and next due date, entry-training date and annual-training completion.
Be able to produce the roster and proof of §§1796.43, .44 and .45 compliance to CDSS on request (§1796.37(a)(5)).
Review the roster monthly. Flag TB exams due within 60 days and annual training due within 60 days. Remove from the schedule any aide whose requirement has lapsed.
